etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English importaunce, from Middle French importance, from Medieval Latin importantia. By surface analysis, import (“to be important”) +‎ -ance.

definitions.definition: The quality or condition of being important or worthy of note.

quote.citation: 1895, Kenneth Graham, The Golden Age, London, page 5:
quote.text: It was incessant matter for amazement how these Olympians would talk over our heads - during meals, for instance - of this or the other social or political inanity, under the delusion that these pale phantasms of reality were among the importances of life.
